-- UTC clock time for a Unix timestamp in seconds.
-- The caller grants no capabilities, so no `uses` clause appears anywhere.

type Hms = { h: int, m: int, s: int }

-- Two-digit, zero-padded decimal for a value in 0..99.
pad2(n: int) -> str =
  pre n >= 0
  pre n < 100
  post out.char_count() == 2
  ex pad2(7) == "07"
  ex pad2(42) == "42"
  if n < 10
    "0\(n)"
  else
    "\(n)"

-- Splits a timestamp into UTC hours, minutes, and seconds (floor arithmetic, so negative values wrap to the previous day).
split(ts: int) -> Hms =
  post out.h >= 0 and out.h < 24
  post out.m >= 0 and out.m < 60
  post out.s >= 0 and out.s < 60
  ex split(0) == Hms(h: 0, m: 0, s: 0)
  ex split(3661) == Hms(h: 1, m: 1, s: 1)
  let secs = ts % 86400
  Hms(h: secs // 3600, m: (secs % 3600) // 60, s: secs % 60)

-- Formats a Unix timestamp in seconds as HH:MM:SS, UTC, 24-hour, zero-padded.
stamp(ts: int) -> str =
  post out.char_count() == 8
  ex stamp(0) == "00:00:00"
  ex stamp(3661) == "01:01:01"
  ex stamp(86399) == "23:59:59"
  let t = split(ts)
  "\(pad2(t.h)):\(pad2(t.m)):\(pad2(t.s))"
